q-78237.name: Question 1
q-78237.problem: Write the equation of the hyperbola $7{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}=56$ in standard form.
q-78237.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $56$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2} & =56 \\ \frac{7{x}^{2}}{56}-\frac{4{y}^{2}}{56} & =\frac{56}{56} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{14} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Write the equation of the hyperbola 7x2−4y2=56 in standard form.

a
x22−y28=1
b
x24−y28=1
c
x216−y212=1
d
x28−y214=1
e
x24−y27=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is x2a2−y2b2=1.

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by 56 and then simplify, as follows:

7x2−4y2=567x256−4y256=5656x28−y214=1

q-78259.name: Question 2
q-78259.problem: Write the equation of the hyperbola $5{y}^{2}-12{x}^{2}=60$ in standard form.
q-78259.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $60$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-12{x}^{2} & =60 \\ \frac{5{y}^{2}}{60}-\frac{12{x}^{2}}{60} & =\frac{60}{60} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{12}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{5} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

q-320673.problem:
The equation of the hyperbola $14{x}^{2}-21{y}^{2}=126$ in standard form is{{field-1}}
$=1.$
q-320673.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $126$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}14{x}^{2}-21{y}^{2} & =126 \\ \frac{14{x}^{2}}{126}-\frac{21{y}^{2}}{126} & =\frac{126}{126} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{6} & =1\end{aligned}
$$
